key_insight: AI-simulated psychotherapy sessions reproduced the expected link between stronger empathy, affirmation, and alliance building and higher motivational interviewing quality ratings.
clinical_relevance: Controlled simulations could complement psychotherapy research, but these findings do not establish benefits for real patients.
method: Linked locally deployed Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct therapist and patient models to generate 512 sessions across eight vignettes and eight therapist personas.
Manipulated therapist prompts to produce high versus low levels of common therapeutic factors.
Evaluated sessions using blinded, repeated LLM ratings and mixed-effects models; human coders rated a stratified subsample.
evidence_signal: Of 512 simulations, 480 were analyzed; high-factor sessions scored higher on all motivational interviewing global ratings (β=0.54–0.95; all p<0.001).
watch_item: LLM-generated interactions and primarily LLM-based ratings may share biases; simulated improvements require validation against human therapy data.
paper_title: Simulating Psychotherapeutic Sessions with Generative Artificial Intelligence: A Proof-of-Concept Study of In Silico Psychotherapy Research
